rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for all reporting owners 2025-05 through 2026-05-25; classify code P (open-market purchase) vs code A (award) vs code F/S (disposition/sale); compute insider buy/sell asymmetry into 28.9% drawdown
rfm_tuples.M_value: 12 months of Form 4s reveal: ONE open-market code-P purchase (Director W. Howard MORRIS, 2026-03-12, 4,050 shares @ ~$129.40 = ~$524K, taking his direct holdings from 407 to 4,307 shares = 10x increase). Zero code-P purchases by any executive officer including CEO Aylward, CFO Angerthal, COO Smirl, CLO Purkalitis, EVP-Distribution Mandinach, EVP-HR Lieberman. Director Susan Fleming sold 6,281 shares total (2025-12-11: 2,959 @ ~$168; 2026-02-11: 3,322 @ ~$142) = ~$1.0M of code-S sales. All May 2026 and March 2026 executive transactions are code A (RSU grants) paired with code F (tax-withholding dispositions) — no voluntary open-market purchases. Buy/sell asymmetry by dollar value: ~$524K buy vs ~$1.0M sell (Fleming). One director conviction is NOT a clustered insider buying signal.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B test: if management truly believed the 29% drawdown is irrational vs intrinsic value, the expected behavior is C-suite code-P open-market buying. Result is the OPPOSITE: CEO/CFO took only RSU awards plus tax-withholding sells in March 2026 (post 10-K, post Keystone close, at $126 — well below mid-2025 levels). The single director purchase (Morris ~$524K) is a positive Mode B finding worth noting, but it is unilateral, not C-suite, and is OUTWEIGHED by Director Fleming's clustered selling immediately before Q4 2025 earnings (Dec 2025) and immediately before the 10-K (Feb 2026). Form 4 evidence contradicts a 'management committed into drawdown' narrative.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: One director's clustered selling, NOT in a 10b5-1 plan, immediately preceding two material capital events and the 10-K. Even if individually defensible, the timing pattern is exactly what the insider_vs_calendar m-source flags as 'opposite of management confidence framing.' Adds asymmetric weight to the negative side of the Form 4 read.

summary: VRTS FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q show accelerating AUM outflows (-$8.4B Q1 2026 vs -$3.0B Q1 2025, -180% YoY) in a year when average AUM declined 4.3% despite S&P +16%, implying severe relative underperformance and share loss. Debt grew 68% to fund private-credit pivot (Keystone $200M+$170M; Crescent Cove $41M) and capital return ($60M buyback, dividend raised to $2.40) while operating cash flow turned NEGATIVE $67M. Form 4 evidence is asymmetric and mixed: ONE meaningful director open-market purchase (Morris ~$524K, 10x his prior position) is positive, but ZERO C-suite code-P purchases and Director Fleming's clustered NON-10b5-1 selling immediately before Q4 earnings and the 10-K work in the opposite direction. Disclosure quality is HONEST throughout (no concealment); business trajectory is the issue. Honesty-alpha framework says detecting honestly disclosed bad news is not alpha by itself — but the combination of accelerating organic outflows, operating cash burn, leveraged pivot, and absence of C-suite buying conviction tilts to SHORT-tier rather than NEUTRAL.
